subject.title: fix(models): clear stale auth cooldowns after early limit resets

question: Should OpenClaw make `models auth clear-cooldown <profile-id>` the supported operator escape hatch for early provider recovery, rather than requiring a guided Doctor/UI path or relying solely on automatic probes?
rationale: The code can be assessed mechanically, but selecting a permanent public command that mutates persisted provider availability state—and deciding whether terminal-only recovery is adequate—requires maintainer product intent.

options.title: Adopt the explicit reset
options.body: Approve the profile-scoped command after redacted end-to-end evidence proves it clears only the intended state and restores normal routing after a safe restart.

options.title: Move to guided recovery
options.body: Pause this command and provide the same narrowly scoped reset through Doctor or an in-product recovery flow for users without shell access.

options.title: Rely on automatic recovery
options.body: Close this PR if maintainers want early recovery handled only by automatic provider probes and existing fallback behavior.

recommendation.title: Adopt the explicit reset
recommendation.body: Approve the profile-scoped command after redacted end-to-end evidence proves it clears only the intended state and restores normal routing after a safe restart.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal combines major auth-profile state work with merger responsibility for related cooldown behavior.
